  • [x] Check that the budgeted flow remains compatible with existing clients.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] No failures on empty or near-empty retrieval results.
  • [x] Existing API/MCP contracts remain stable.
  • [x] The budgeted output is predictable in tests.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• [x] Unit tests for budget selection and overflow handling.
  • [x] API/MCP tests for backward compatibility.
  • [x] Regression tests for empty-result and low-budget cases.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• [x] memory_ask returns concise answers within a defined token budget.
  • [x] Citations remain accurate.
  • [x] Existing clients continue to work without changes.

docs.title: Conversation Grouping Plan
docs.text:
Source date: 28-05-2026

Status: implemented

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Improve how related chunks from the same conversation are surfaced so grouped context is easier to consume.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• [x] Add conversation-level scoring.
  • [x] Ensure chunks from the same conversation can be grouped or prioritized together.
  • [x] Keep this focused on grouping behavior rather than search precision in general.

docs.title: Phase 1: Scoring model
docs.text:
• [x] Define how conversation-level score should be computed.
  • [x] Decide whether it acts as a boost, a grouping signal, or both.
  • [x] Keep the per-chunk score visible so the behavior stays explainable.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] The grouping/scoring rule is clearly defined.
  • [x] Related chunks can be identified as belonging together.
  • [x] The score model does not obscure the base retrieval signal.

docs.title: Phase 2: Group-aware ranking
docs.text:
• [x] Apply conversation-level scoring after the base retrieval step.
  • [x] Prefer sets of chunks that form a coherent conversation when appropriate.
  • [x] Keep unrelated but individually strong chunks from being incorrectly merged.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] Chunks from the same conversation are surfaced together when relevant.
  • [x] Strong unrelated matches are not accidentally suppressed.
  • [x] Ranking remains stable and understandable.

docs.title: Phase 3: Output validation
docs.text:
• [x] Ensure grouped results remain compatible with memory_ask.
  • [x] Confirm citations and summaries still point to the correct underlying chunks.
  • [x] Keep the grouping behavior optional or conservative if needed.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] memory_ask can consume grouped context without breaking output shape.
  • [x] Citations remain accurate at the chunk level.
  • [x] Grouping improves readability without damaging precision.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• [x] Unit tests for conversation score calculation.
  • [x] Retrieval tests for grouped results from the same conversation.
  • [x] Regression tests to ensure unrelated results are not over-grouped.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• [x] Related chunks are surfaced together more consistently.
  • [x] The grouped view improves readability of search/ask output.
  • [x] Existing result accuracy is preserved.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Implemented in memory.ingestion.mvp_ingestion.search, group_conversation_results, and _apply_result_mode.
  • conversation_score is the best score for a conversation group, and conversation_match_count exposes how many chunks matched.
  • Grouping is conservative: only chunks within the configured conversation score window are grouped ahead of unrelated matches.
  • result_mode supports chunks, compact, and conversations through CLI, HTTP, MCP search, and MCP ask paths.

docs.title: Edge Case Test Coverage Plan
docs.text: This plan tracks public-contract edge cases that are not fully covered by the current unit, integration, E2E, and Bruno suites.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Prove API and MCP surfaces interoperate over the same runtime and storage boundaries.
  • Lock down degraded storage behavior for metadata and vector providers.
  • Make auth-mode transitions explicit so local development convenience does not accidentally become a data exposure path.
  • Add regression tests for error paths that are realistic in Docker, LAN, and real-client MCP use.

docs.title: Current Coverage Snapshot
docs.text:
Implemented coverage already includes:

  • HTTP API insert, search, retrieve, ask, facts, profile, bearer auth, OAuth resource-server auth, and shared-project behavior.
  • MCP protocol initialize, session handling, tools/list pagination, prompt and resource listing, and MCP tool handler behavior.
  • MCP client-shaped payload compatibility for Codex, Gemini, Copilot, ChatGPT, and opencode-style payloads.
  • Storage provider contracts, live provider gates, vector fallback startup behavior, metadata startup failure, schema invariants, dimension checks, dry run, and secret redaction.
  • Bruno black-box API and MCP smoke flows against a running service.

Main gaps are cross-surface workflows, auth-mode transition behavior, mid-run provider failure behavior, and explicit negative cases for degraded state.

docs.title: P0: API And MCP Cross-Surface Workflows
docs.text:
Add tests proving API and MCP are interchangeable clients for the same memory store.

  • [x] API insert, MCP search, MCP retrieve, MCP ask.
  • [x] MCP insert, API search, API retrieve, API ask.
  • [x] API insert with project_id, MCP read with the same project_id.
  • [x] MCP insert with project_id, API read with the same project_id.
  • [x] API bearer-token insert, MCP bearer-token read under the same owner.
  • [x] MCP bearer-token insert, API bearer-token read under the same owner.
  • [x] Two MCP sessions shaped as Codex and opencode clients using the same bearer token can each insert memory and read the other session's memory.
  • [x] The same Codex/opencode MCP sessions using different bearer tokens cannot retrieve or search each other's private default-project memory.
  • [x] Cross-owner negative checks for both directions: API writes must not leak through MCP reads, and MCP writes must not leak through API reads.
  • [x] Response-shape equivalence checks for shared fields: status, id, results, memory, answer, citations, confidence, and answer_basis.

Implemented in tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py. Note: MCP search exposes cursor; HTTP API search currently does not, so the interop test checks cursor on MCP and compares the actual shared public fields across both surfaces.

Preferred location:

  • tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py

Use TestClient against create_app(config={"interfaces": {"api": True, "mcp": True}}) so both surfaces share one agent/runtime.

docs.title: P0: Two-Agent MCP Bearer Interop
docs.text:
Expected policy:

  • MCP session identity and clientInfo.name must not define data ownership.
  • Bearer token ownership defines private default-project visibility.
  • Two agents that intentionally share one bearer token share the same owner boundary and can read each other's memory.
  • Two agents using different bearer tokens stay isolated unless they use an explicit shared project with allowed membership.

Implemented deterministic coverage:

  • [x] A Codex-shaped MCP session and an opencode-shaped MCP session initialize with the same bearer token, each call memory_insert, and both can retrieve and search the inserted memories.
  • [x] The same client-shaped sessions initialize with different bearer tokens, each can retrieve its own memory, and neither can retrieve or search the other owner's private memory.

This is intentionally a deterministic integration test instead of a required real Codex/opencode plus Ollama CI gate. Real client binaries, local model configuration, and headless CLI command syntax are operational smoke concerns; this P0 regression locks down the hub contract that auth scope and owner isolation follow tokens and projects, not agent names.

Preferred location:

  • tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py

docs.title: P0: Storage Outage And Fallback Policy
docs.text:
Expected policy:

  • Metadata provider startup failure is fatal. Do not fallback from Postgres or MongoDB metadata to SQLite or in-memory metadata.
  • Vector provider startup failure may fallback to in-memory vectors only when storage.vector.allow_fallback: true.
  • Runtime health must report degraded state when vector fallback is active.
  • Secrets must never appear in health reasons, logs, API responses, or MCP tool errors.

Add or verify tests:

  • [x] Postgres metadata unavailable at startup fails app/runtime creation.
  • [x] Redis vector unavailable at startup with allow_fallback=false fails app/runtime creation.
  • [x] Redis vector unavailable at startup with allow_fallback=true starts in degraded mode and reports requested_vector_provider=redis, vector_provider=memory, and vector_fallback_active=true.
  • [x] PGVector unavailable at startup follows the same disabled/enabled fallback policy.
  • [x] Degraded vector fallback does not claim durable vector persistence.
  • [x] API /ready reflects degraded vector state consistently.
  • [x] MCP memory://health reflects degraded vector state consistently.
  • [x] Provider credentials are redacted in startup exceptions, health reasons, and MCP/API error envelopes.

Preferred locations:

  • Startup and provider policy: tests/integration/test_storage_features.py
  • API/MCP health exposure: tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py

Follow-up candidate:

  • [x] Add mid-run outage tests with fake providers that fail on insert or search. Startup fallback does not cover this case. Runtime operation failures should return deterministic API/MCP errors and should not silently switch providers after writes have started. Covered by tests/integration/test_midrun_provider_failures.py.

docs.title: P0: Auth-Mode Transition Behavior
docs.text:
Question: if a user writes data while auth is enabled, then the server restarts with api.auth: none, should that data be readable without credentials?

Expected answer: no for user-scoped data. auth=none may be used for CI/test-fixture data and unauthenticated local-default test data, but it should not become a credential bypass for rows previously stamped with an authenticated owner or a non-local project.

The current implementation resolves unauthenticated requests to the local default project and denies explicit access to non-local projects. Add tests to lock this down.

Add tests:

  • [x] Bearer-token insert into owner default project, restart/recreate app with the same persistent store and api.auth: none, unauthenticated API search returns no owner-scoped result.
  • [x] Same scenario for unauthenticated API retrieve by ID returns 404.
  • [x] Same scenario for unauthenticated API ask does not use owner-scoped facts or conversations.
  • [x] Same scenario through MCP search, retrieve, and ask.
  • [x] Explicit project_id for the authenticated owner's default project is rejected under auth=none.
  • [x] OAuth resource-server insert using sub=owner-a, restart/recreate app with auth=none, unauthenticated API/MCP reads do not return owner-scoped data.
  • [x] Authenticated shared-project data is not readable under auth=none unless the project is the synthetic local-default project.
  • [x] Existing unauthenticated local-default data remains readable after restart with auth=none.

Preferred location:

  • tests/integration/test_auth_mode_transitions.py

Use SQLite metadata and a temporary vector store path so restart behavior uses real persistence, not only in-process stubs.

docs.title: P1: Payload, Validation, And Injection Edges
docs.text:
Existing tests cover invalid schemas, malformed MCP payloads, invalid IDs, and some injection-like IDs. Add cross-surface negative cases:

  • [x] API accepts no client-supplied owner_id; server stamps authenticated owner.
  • [x] MCP accepts no client-supplied owner_id; server stamps authenticated owner.
  • [x] API and MCP reject invalid project_id formats consistently.
  • [x] API and MCP reject unknown result_mode consistently.
  • [x] API and MCP cap or reject extreme top_k, limit, and max_context_tokens consistently.
  • [x] API and MCP preserve date/tag/thread filters consistently.
  • [x] Tool and API error messages remain actionable but do not include payload text, credentials, full queries, or provider URLs with secrets.

docs.title: P1: Deduplication And Append Across Surfaces
docs.text:
Add tests for mixed client workflows:

  • [x] API inserts a conversation, MCP retries the same conversation and gets the deduplicated result.
  • [x] MCP inserts a conversation, API retries the same conversation and gets the deduplicated result.
  • [x] API inserts an initial thread, MCP appends messages using the same upstream thread metadata.
  • [x] MCP inserts an initial thread, API appends messages using the same upstream thread metadata.
  • [x] Same-id/different-content conflicts return deterministic errors through both surfaces.
  • [x] Same conversation hash in different projects is allowed and remains isolated.

docs.title: P1: Facts And Profile Cross-Surface Behavior
docs.text:
Add tests proving the fact layer obeys the same boundaries:

  • [x] API insert extracts facts, MCP profile/fact search can read them under the same owner/project.
  • [x] MCP insert extracts facts, API profile/fact endpoints can read them under the same owner/project.
  • [x] Cross-owner fact/profile queries do not leak facts.
  • [x] auth=none cannot read owner-scoped facts created under bearer or OAuth auth.
  • [x] Supersession through one surface is visible through the other.

docs.title: P1: Multilingual And Embedding Model Drift
docs.text:
Expected policy:

  • ai-memory-hub should not declare English-only behavior. The hub stores and searches Unicode text, and multilingual retrieval should work when the configured embedding model supports the languages involved.
  • Multilingual quality is an embedding-model capability, not an API/MCP contract special case.
  • The same configured embedding provider, model, dimension, and embedding options must be used for both ingestion and query-time retrieval.
  • Changing the embedding model, dimension, provider, or model options for an existing vector index requires an explicit reindex or a separate vector namespace/index. Do not silently mix vectors from different embedding spaces.

Current guardrails:

  • Different dimensions are caught by startup and runtime vector dimensionality checks.
  • Same-dimension model swaps are not reliably detectable from vector shape alone and can silently degrade or corrupt retrieval ranking.

Add tests and implementation checks:

  • [x] English insert, English query works with the configured model.
  • [x] Non-English insert, same-language query works when using the same multilingual-capable test embedder.
  • [x] Non-English insert, English query works only as a model-quality smoke test, not as a deterministic correctness guarantee.
  • [x] Unicode normalization edge cases do not crash ingestion, hashing, chunking, search, ask, facts, or profile extraction.
  • [x] Startup records embedding provider, model, dimension, and relevant options as vector-index metadata where the provider supports it.
  • [x] Startup fails or enters an explicit "reindex required" state when existing vector-index metadata does not match the configured embedding provider/model, even if dimensions match.
  • [x] API and MCP health expose the active embedding provider/model/dimension and any embedding-index mismatch state without leaking provider credentials.
  • [x] Reindex command or runbook is documented before allowing a configured model swap on persistent vector stores.

Preferred locations:

  • Embedding/index compatibility: tests/integration/test_storage_features.py
  • Public health exposure: tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py
  • Unicode and cross-language public behavior: tests/integration/test_api_mcp_interop.py

docs.title: P2: Operational And Observability Edges
docs.text:
Add tests or smoke checks for:

  • [x] /health and /ready remain public and secret-free under every auth mode.
  • [x] MCP protected-resource metadata remains public and secret-free in OAuth mode.
  • [x] Request failures emit structured logs without payload, token, query, or DSN leakage.
  • [x] Startup logs clearly state fallback policy and dry-run state.
  • [x] Production-oriented config with allow_fallback=true emits a warning once that fallback may make vector data non-durable.

docs.title: Suggested Execution Order
docs.text:
1. Add test_api_mcp_interop.py with unauthenticated cross-surface happy paths.
  2. Extend it with bearer-token cross-surface isolation.
  3. Add test_auth_mode_transitions.py using persistent SQLite/LanceDB temp storage.
  4. Fill Redis and PGVector outage assertions in existing storage tests.
  5. Add embedding-index compatibility checks for model/provider/dimension drift.
  6. Add cross-surface fact/profile and dedupe/append regressions.
  7. Add mid-run fake-provider failure tests after startup behavior is locked down.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• Every public memory operation is covered in both directions: API -> MCP and MCP -> API.
  • Authenticated data is not exposed by restarting with api.auth: none.
  • Metadata provider outages fail startup; vector provider outages only fallback when explicitly allowed.
  • Multilingual retrieval is documented as model-dependent, and persistent vector stores cannot silently mix same-dimension vectors from different embedding models.
  • Degraded mode is observable from health surfaces and never silently changes response contracts.
  • No edge-case test exposes secrets or sensitive payloads in failures.

docs.title: Efficiency Revival Plan
docs.text: Source date: 25-10-2026

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Make ai-memory-hub cheaper and faster to operate without weakening retrieval quality, authorization, durability, privacy, or deterministic fallbacks.

Efficiency means improving all of the following together:

  • end-to-end latency for insert, search, retrieve, ask, and import;
  • useful work per embedding, storage call, candidate, byte, and model token;
  • throughput under concurrent ingestion and retrieval;
  • resident memory, database growth, index growth, and temporary allocations;
  • startup, readiness, maintenance, and CI cost; and
  • operator effort required to diagnose slow or wasteful behavior.

This is a measurement-first plan. An optimization is complete only when a before/after report shows a material gain and the existing quality and safety gates still pass.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Do not trade recall, fact correctness, provenance, or tenant isolation for a lower latency number.
  • Do not introduce a mandatory hosted cache, queue, model, or telemetry service.
  • Do not cache raw private conversation payloads outside the configured stores.
  • Do not optimize every supported provider identically; use capability-aware paths and retain bounded fallbacks.
  • Do not change public HTTP or MCP response shapes solely for performance.

docs.title: Current Baseline And Evidence
docs.text:
The following local measurements are directional baselines from one Windows development machine on 25-10-2026; they are not cross-platform service-level objectives.

Benchmark Current local result Planning implication Config parsing 1.43 ms average over 200 warm iterations Cache only immutable, path-keyed runtime configuration; first prove it repeats on request paths. Schema loading 0.66 ms average over 200 warm iterations A path-and-mtime-aware schema cache may help validation-heavy ingestion. Token counting 0.03 ms warm average Encoding initialization is already cached; text-level caching is low priority unless real traces show repeated identical text. Schema compatibility 0.01 ms average Do not optimize this independently. Default ask 2.41 ms average in the deterministic benchmark Preserve as the local comparison path. Request-level 80-token budget 3.06 ms, 1.27x default latency The extra CPU is acceptable only when it reduces downstream context or model cost. Config-enabled 80-token budget 2.77 ms, 1.15x default latency Prefer one configured budget over repeated per-client policy decisions. Selected ask context 8 chunks down to 2 chunks / 75 tokens Measure total model latency and token cost, not only local selection overhead.

The token-budget benchmark also emitted an audit persistence exception for each measured request because its stub store cannot retain fallback audit events. That repeated exception logging pollutes profiles and adds avoidable CPU and I/O. Benchmark and test doubles must support a silent bounded audit sink before their results are trusted for optimization decisions.

Existing observability already measures API, MCP, ingestion-stage, embedding, and vector-search durations. Existing benchmark coverage includes token budgets, cache candidates, retrieval quality, graph quality, and the versioned retrieval/extraction quality gate. The plan should extend these assets instead of creating a separate performance framework.

docs.title: Efficiency Scorecard
docs.text: Every performance report should identify the deployment profile, corpus size, provider versions, cold/warm state, concurrency, and machine class.

docs.title: Latency
docs.text:
• insert, append, search, retrieve, ask, and import p50/p95/p99;
  • embedding and vector-search p50/p95 separately;
  • query planning, lexical search, fact search, fusion, reranking, context assembly, audit persistence, and serialization duration;
  • cold startup and readiness time; and
  • first request versus steady-state latency.

docs.title: Work Amplification
docs.text:
• embedding requests and embedded chunks per accepted conversation;
  • vector candidates fetched per returned result;
  • filtered-search attempts and candidates discarded after retrieval;
  • metadata reads and rows loaded per request;
  • facts, graph records, and summaries scanned per answer;
  • audit writes and log records per operation; and
  • context tokens supplied per cited or answer-supporting token.

docs.title: Capacity And Cost
docs.text:
• conversations and messages ingested per second;
  • queries per second at concurrency 1, 4, 16, and 32;
  • peak and steady-state resident memory;
  • metadata and vector bytes per conversation and per chunk;
  • model calls, input tokens, output tokens, and estimated provider cost; and
  • background maintenance duration and temporary disk use.

docs.title: Mandatory Guardrails
docs.text:
• the versioned quality gate remains green;
  • filtered recall, precision@1, recall@k, MRR, nDCG, fact precision/recall, temporal accuracy, and fallback accuracy do not regress beyond an approved tolerance;
  • authorization/project isolation and secret-redaction tests remain green;
  • no unbounded cache, queue, candidate list, retry loop, or log stream; and
  • rollback is configuration-only or a small isolated code revert.

docs.title: Target Deployment Profiles
docs.text:
Use three profiles so local optimizations do not accidentally penalize larger deployments.

Profile Representative setup Primary constraint Local SQLite + LanceDB/local embeddings, one user startup, memory, idle cost, simple operations Team Postgres + PGVector or Qdrant, 4–32 concurrent clients throughput, pooling, tenant fairness Remote-provider hosted metadata/vector/model services round trips, batching, retries, token and request cost

Each optimization must state which profiles benefit and which may regress.

docs.title: Phase 0: Make Measurements Trustworthy
docs.text:
Deliver this phase before changing production algorithms.

  • [ ] Fix benchmark/test audit sinks so expected unsupported persistence does not emit exception traces per request.
  • [ ] Add a request-scoped work ledger to benchmark reports: storage calls, embedding calls/texts, candidate counts, filtered candidates, reranker calls, audit writes, selected chunks, and context tokens.
  • [ ] Add cold/warm separation and p50/p95/p99 output to performance helpers; averages alone hide tail regressions.
  • [ ] Add reproducible synthetic corpora at small, medium, and large scales, including high-selectivity and low-selectivity filters.
  • [ ] Add concurrency runners for insert, search, and ask without external credentials.
  • [ ] Persist machine-readable before/after reports as CI artifacts.
  • [ ] Keep deterministic CI gates short; run provider load profiles on demand or on a scheduled workflow.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Repeated benchmark runs on an idle machine have documented variance bounds.
  • Profiles contain no repeated expected exception logging.
  • A report can attribute a regression to a stage or amplification counter, not only to total request time.
  • Performance fixtures contain synthetic data only.

Implementation status:

  • The first benchmark-hygiene slice adds a bounded audit sink to the token budget benchmark, separates first-call and warm latency, reports warm average/p50/p95/p99/min/max distributions, and records per-request search, candidate, audit-write, and result/context amplification. Cache-candidate operations now report first-call and warm percentile distributions. Scale corpora, concurrency runners, broader provider work ledgers, and persisted CI comparison artifacts remain follow-up work.

docs.title: Phase 1: Remove Request-Path Waste
docs.text:
Start with low-risk work that should not alter ranking or storage semantics.

  • [x] Trace config parsing and schema loading to confirm whether they occur on hot request paths.
  • [x] If repeated, cache parsed configuration by resolved path plus file identity and invalidate explicitly on reload.
  • [x] If repeated, cache validated schemas by resolved path plus modification time; never allow one configured schema to contaminate another runtime.
  • [ ] Reuse bounded provider clients and connection pools rather than creating network clients per operation.
  • [x] Compute normalized conversation/search text once per candidate within a request and reuse it across lexical, metadata, fact, and boost stages.
  • [x] Replace repeated single-record lookups with existing get_many or a new provider capability only where traces show N+1 behavior.
  • [ ] Avoid building detailed diagnostics, provenance projections, or full result bodies when the caller requested a concise response.
  • [ ] Bound and deduplicate warning/error logs by failure class while retaining counters and first-occurrence diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria:

  • At least one measured hot-path cost is removed or the phase closes with evidence that the suspected work is not material.
  • Warm p95 latency improves by at least 10% on an affected path, or total work amplification drops by at least 20%.
  • Cache invalidation and multi-config tests pass.
  • No raw payload, query, embedding, token, or secret is added to cache keys or logs.

Implementation note (runtime immutable-data cache slice): tracing confirmed that configuration parsing and schema file loading occur during runtime construction rather than on normal request paths, so parsed configuration is intentionally left uncached. Payload validation did, however, re-check and recompile the same schema for every ingest. Runtimes now reuse a checked validator cached by resolved schema path, nanosecond modification time, and file size; the cache is bounded to 16 identities and supports explicit invalidation. Direct schema loads remain isolated so caller mutation cannot contaminate another runtime. On a 100-iteration local synthetic run, reusing the validator reduced unprofiled validation p95 from 29.60 ms to 0.33 ms (more than 98%); exact timings are environment-dependent. Invalidation, mutation isolation, and multi-schema tests cover reload and concurrent configuration safety.

Implementation note (fact-source batch hydration slice): fact filtering, text ranking, temporal projection, retrieval-candidate construction, and provenance assembly now deduplicate source conversation IDs and reuse bounded get_many reads. Batches are capped at 500 IDs to match every metadata provider contract, while custom stores without get_many retain the compatible single-read fallback. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.fact_hydration_efficiency fixture preserves all 120 fact results while reducing the former 240 source reads across ranking and public projection to one batch read for three unique conversations (more than 99% fewer metadata read calls). No conversation payloads are cached across requests.

Implementation note (request-local search-text reuse slice): fact ranking and question narrowing now share each hydrated source conversation's assembled search text for the duration of that operation. The cache uses in-memory object identity, is discarded after the request stage, and never stores text across requests. Lexical candidates already assembled their conversation text once per candidate. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.search_text_efficiency fixture preserves all 120 ranked facts while reducing source conversation search-text construction from 120 times to three times for three unique conversations (97.5% less construction work).

docs.title: Phase 2: Make Ingestion Proportional To New Information
docs.text:
• [ ] Establish stage timings and amplification counts for validate, normalize, hash, deduplicate, chunk, extract, embed, metadata write, vector write, derived-record write, and audit.
  • [x] Complete deduplication and append-delta detection before embedding or derived extraction wherever the contract permits.
  • [x] Batch embedding inputs up to provider-advertised limits with bounded payload size and deterministic result-to-chunk mapping.
  • [ ] Use metadata/vector batch-write capabilities when available; retain the current atomic or compensating behavior on partial failure.
  • [ ] Introduce bounded ingestion concurrency by project/provider, with backpressure rather than unbounded task creation.
  • [ ] Avoid recomputing facts, graph records, summaries, or hashes for unchanged messages during append and reindex.
  • [ ] Add checkpointed, resumable reindex batches so a large reindex does not retain the entire corpus or restart from zero.
  • [x] Report bytes and rows written per accepted message and per duplicate.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Duplicate ingestion performs zero embedding and vector-write work.
  • Append work scales with new messages/chunks rather than full conversation length.
  • Batch ingestion improves remote-provider throughput by at least 25% without increasing error leakage or partial-write ambiguity.
  • Peak memory remains bounded by configured batch size.

Implementation note (duplicate-ingestion fast-path slice): exact duplicates now return before summary/fact/graph derivation, metadata rewrites, embedding, or vector writes when the stored manifest is indexed and the vector provider confirms all expected chunk IDs. Pending manifests are reconciled from existing vector rows, while missing vectors retain the full repair path. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.ingestion_efficiency work ledger reports calls, rows, and bytes for accepted and duplicate inputs. Its baseline fixture drops from two embedding inputs and two vector-row writes on the former full-reindex path to zero of each, a 100% reduction; the required audit row remains.

Implementation note (single-pass append-summary slice): generated summaries are now attached only after trusted-append detection. New conversations retain the same summary behavior, while an append generates summaries once from the combined stored conversation instead of first writing transient summaries for the incoming transcript and immediately overwriting the same derived identities. The deterministic ingestion work ledger preserves the final three-message summary and reduces the append fixture from two summary passes and four derived-row writes to one pass and two writes (50% less summary work). Rejected same-ID updates also perform no generated-summary writes. Other unchanged-message derivation remains follow-up work.

Implementation note (incremental append-graph slice): trusted appends now run graph extraction only over newly appended messages and carry the original zero-based message offset into entity and relationship provenance. Existing relationships remain available for conflict supersession, while unchanged messages are not scanned or rewritten by the extraction stage. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.append_graph_efficiency fixture reduces graph inputs for a two-message conversation plus one-message append from three messages to one (66.7%) and verifies that the new relationship still cites message index 2. Facts were already append-incremental; unchanged-message hashing and reindex work remain follow-up items.

Implementation note (verified append-identity reuse slice): normalization still recomputes every client-supplied message hash so trusted appends cannot bypass integrity checks. When the normalized payload contains the complete stored prefix plus its append, the write path now reuses that already verified, project-scoped aggregate conversation identity instead of joining and hashing the same ordered hashes a second time. Sibling-thread continuations retain a safe combined-history recomputation and now preserve project scoping. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.append_hash_efficiency fixture reduces aggregate hash passes and message-hash scans for a 64-message conversation plus one-message append from two/130 to one/65 (50%). Per-message normalization and broader unchanged-message derivation remain follow-up work.

Implementation note (bounded embedding-batch slice): remote embedding inputs are now split sequentially by configured count and serialized UTF-8 JSON input bytes before provider calls. Vector persistence begins only after every batch succeeds, so a later provider failure cannot expose a partial vector write. HTTP response indexes are validated and restored to request order when present; legacy unindexed responses retain their declared order. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.embedding_batch_efficiency fixture preserves all ten chunk/vector mappings while reducing the largest request from ten inputs to three (70%); its four batches remain at or below both advertised limits. Bounded concurrency and remote-provider throughput measurements remain follow-up work.

docs.title: Phase 3: Reduce Retrieval Amplification
docs.text:
• [ ] Break search and ask latency into planning, embedding, dense, lexical, fact, graph, fusion, reranking, hydration, context, and serialization.
  • [ ] Run independent candidate sources concurrently only when provider clients are safe and a shared deadline can cancel or ignore late optional work.
  • [ ] Make candidate limits responsive to top_k, filter selectivity, provider pushdown capability, and observed hit yield; retain hard global caps.
  • [ ] Hydrate only unique candidate IDs and only fields required by the selected response mode and reranker projection.
  • [ ] Skip semantic reranking when deterministic evidence is decisive, the candidate set is too small to change order, or the remaining deadline is insufficient.
  • [ ] Reuse the query plan between memory_lookup, search, and ask sub-steps inside one request; do not cache authorization scope from model output.
  • [ ] Add a bounded, privacy-safe query-embedding cache only after production traces demonstrate meaningful exact-query repetition. Key it by embedding provider/model/version and normalized query, never by incomplete tenant scope when results are cached.
  • [ ] Prefer fact/profile or summary evidence before raw chunks when it answers the question with equal or better confidence and provenance.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Candidate-to-result amplification falls by at least 25% on filtered and unfiltered medium/large corpora.
  • Search and ask p95 improve by at least 20% for one target profile.
  • Reranker/model call rate drops without reducing fallback accuracy or quality metrics.
  • Deadline and cancellation behavior is deterministic and test-covered.

Implementation note (adaptive candidate-budget slice): unfiltered lexical and fact candidate admission now uses the smaller of each configured hard cap and top_k * candidate_multiplier, matching the existing dense-search budget. Filtered and non-active-memory searches retain their configured maxima because some metadata providers apply those constraints after their initial text limit. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.retrieval_amplification fixture reduces the representative top_k=5, multiplier-3 lexical/fact budget from 75 to 30 candidates (60%) while preserving the full 75-candidate filtered budget. The versioned quality gate retains perfect precision@1, recall@k, MRR, nDCG, filtered recall, temporal accuracy, and fallback accuracy on its synthetic corpus. Provider-pushdown and observed-yield adaptation remain follow-up work.

Implementation note (small-set reranker-bypass slice): rank fusion now reports insufficient_candidates and skips both bounded projection construction and semantic reranker invocation when its rerankable subset contains zero or one candidate. A single candidate cannot change relative order, including when a configured reranker batch limit exposes only the leading item. Multi-candidate semantic, timeout, error, and deterministic-fallback paths are unchanged. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.reranker_efficiency fixture reduces the single-candidate reranker call count from one to zero (100%), preserves the result, and verifies that a two-candidate request still makes one call. The versioned quality gate remains green with unchanged retrieval metrics.

docs.title: Phase 4: Bound Context And Model Cost
docs.text:
• [ ] Measure input/output tokens and selected evidence per ask mode and client.
  • [ ] Define default context budgets by concise/detailed response mode, with explicit overrides and stable diagnostics.
  • [x] Deduplicate overlapping chunks before token counting and context assembly.
  • [ ] Prefer the smallest evidence span that preserves the claim and citation.
  • [ ] Use existing summaries and validated facts as compact evidence; never synthesize a summary merely to save tokens unless its creation cost and provenance are accounted for.
  • [ ] Gate optional planner, extractor, reranker, and answer-model calls with deterministic sufficiency checks.
  • [ ] Track model calls avoided, tokens avoided, and answer quality together.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Median selected context tokens fall by at least 30% on detailed ask cases or at least 50% on concise cases.
  • Total answer latency or provider cost improves after including local token selection overhead.
  • Citation completeness and answer-contract accuracy remain unchanged.

Implementation note (overlapping-context deduplication slice): budgeted ask, fact/chunk arbitration, and handoff context now remove an exact suffix/prefix overlap only when adjacent chunks share both a conversation ID and stored source message hash. Ranking and citation identities remain unchanged, and different messages retain repeated wording. The deterministic memory.benchmarks.context_overlap_efficiency fixture preserves all unique evidence while reducing total selected-context accounting from 40 to 38 tokens (5%); citation framing accounts for the invariant portion of that measurement.

docs.title: Phase 5: Storage And Index Efficiency
docs.text:
• [ ] Capture query plans and row counts for SQLite and Postgres metadata paths used by search, fact/profile reads, timeline, audit, and project scoping.
  • [ ] Add or adjust indexes only for measured scans; include write and storage cost in the before/after report.
  • [ ] Enforce cursor pagination and projection reads on potentially unbounded list/search paths.
  • [ ] Measure index-chunk manifest, fact, graph, audit, and tombstone growth per conversation.
  • [ ] Define safe retention/compaction for superseded derived records, stale pending items, and audit data without altering immutable source memories.
  • [ ] Document provider-specific vacuum, compaction, index-readiness, and connection-pool guidance.
  • [ ] Add health diagnostics for pool saturation, index lag, storage growth, fallback activation, and maintenance age.

Acceptance criteria:

  • The large corpus has no unapproved full scan on critical read paths.
  • Metadata and vector growth remain within documented per-conversation budgets.
  • Maintenance is resumable, bounded, observable, and safe to interrupt.
  • Storage optimizations pass SQLite, Postgres, and relevant provider contracts.

docs.title: Phase 6: Runtime And Operational Efficiency
docs.text:
• [ ] Audit synchronous provider calls executed on async API/MCP paths and move blocking work behind an appropriate bounded execution boundary.
  • [ ] Define connection, worker, queue, batch, timeout, and retry budgets per deployment profile.
  • [ ] Use one end-to-end request deadline; prevent nested retries from exceeding it.
  • [ ] Add overload behavior that fails predictably or sheds optional work before memory and queues grow without bound.
  • [ ] Separate readiness checks from expensive provider probes with bounded, stale-aware caching.
  • [ ] Reduce CI duplication by identifying equivalent push and pull-request runs while preserving branch-protection evidence.
  • [ ] Publish a compact efficiency dashboard/runbook using existing metrics.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Load tests show bounded queue depth and memory at the documented concurrency ceiling.
  • Provider outage tests complete within the request deadline and do not create retry storms.
  • Idle local deployments retain a small, documented resource footprint.
  • CI minutes decrease without removing required test, security, or quality coverage.

docs.title: Proposed PR-Sized Workstreams
docs.text:
Implement in this order; each item should remain independently reviewable.

  1. Benchmark hygiene and work ledger — fix audit-log amplification, add counters, percentiles, cold/warm modes, and synthetic scale profiles.
  2. Runtime immutable-data caches — prove and optimize repeated config/schema work with explicit invalidation.
  3. Incremental and batched ingestion — dedupe before expensive work, batch embeddings/writes, and bound concurrency.
  4. Retrieval amplification controls — stage timings, adaptive candidate limits, unique hydration, and deadline-aware optional work.
  5. Context and model-call economy — evidence dedupe, response-mode budgets, and deterministic model bypasses.
  6. Metadata query/index audit — measured indexes, projections, pagination, growth budgets, and maintenance guidance.
  7. Provider and concurrency profiles — local/team/remote load reports, pooling, backpressure, deadlines, and outage tests.
  8. Operational efficiency and CI — dashboard/runbook, idle footprint, and duplicate-work reduction.

Do not combine workstreams 2–8 into one optimization PR. Measurement changes from workstream 1 may land together because later before/after reports depend on them.

docs.title: Decision Rules
docs.text:
• Prefer deleting work over making unnecessary work faster.
  • Prefer request-local reuse before cross-request caching.
  • Cache immutable or versioned values; require explicit invalidation for mutable values.
  • Include provider/model/version and relevant policy in cache identities.
  • Never cache authorization decisions or results under a key that omits owner, project, visibility, or data-version scope.
  • Bound every cache by entry count and/or bytes, expose hit/miss/eviction metrics, and test eviction.
  • Parallelize independent I/O only under a shared deadline and concurrency cap.
  • Keep local-first deterministic paths functional when optional services are absent.
  • Reject improvements that move cost to startup, memory, storage, CI, or model usage without showing a favorable total-cost tradeoff.

docs.title: Validation Matrix
docs.text:
Each implementation PR should run the smallest relevant subset first, then the broader gates appropriate to its blast radius.

uv run python -m ruff check memory tests tools
uv run python -m pyright
uv run pytest tests/unit tests/integration -q
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.cache_candidates --iterations 1000
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.ingestion_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.append_graph_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.append_hash_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.embedding_batch_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.reranker_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.retrieval_amplification
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.context_overlap_efficiency
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.token_budget --iterations 200
uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.quality_gate \
  --output reports/quality/quality-gate.json

Add provider contract, live-provider, concurrency, or outage tests when the changed path touches pooling, batching, retries, filtering, persistence, or deadlines. Documentation changes must pass the strict MkDocs build.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• [ ] Baseline and before/after reports exist for all three deployment profiles.
  • [ ] Search and ask p95 improve by at least 20% on a representative medium corpus without quality regression.
  • [ ] Duplicate and append ingestion avoid work proportional to unchanged data.
  • [ ] Remote ingestion throughput improves by at least 25% through measured batching and bounded concurrency.
  • [ ] Candidate-to-result amplification falls by at least 25% on representative filtered and unfiltered queries.
  • [ ] Context/model cost falls by at least 30% on the target ask workload with unchanged citation and answer quality.
  • [ ] Memory, storage growth, queue depth, retries, cache size, and maintenance work all have explicit bounds and diagnostics.
  • [ ] Local-first operation, provider fallbacks, auth isolation, redaction, durability, and public contracts remain intact.
  • [ ] The quality gate, full unit/integration suite, provider contracts, and applicable end-to-end tests pass.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Prevent MCP clients from silently persisting personal facts or conversations unless the user explicitly asked to save them, confirmed the save, or intentionally enabled client auto-save.

This comes from real opencode MCP use: the user said they had a yellow Squier Tele with a black pickguard and Nocaster pickups. opencode proactively called memory_insert even though the user had not asked it to save the fact. ai-memory-hub did not scrape the chat; it accepted the tool call the client sent. The server needs a policy option for users who want stronger consent boundaries.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
memory_insert currently trusts the calling client. That is simple and compatible, but it means an agent can decide that ordinary conversation text is memory-worthy and persist it without a clear user action.

Risks:

  • Personal facts can be saved when the user expected transient chat only.
  • Different clients may have different implicit memory behavior.
  • The server cannot distinguish explicit user intent from client auto-save.
  • Users cannot enforce a consent policy centrally across Codex, opencode, Claude, Copilot, or other MCP clients.

docs.title: Current Behavior
docs.text:
• memory_insert accepts API and MCP inserts that pass validation.
  • The server stamps ownership and project scope, but it does not require a save-intent marker.
  • Fact extraction may then turn the inserted conversation into durable facts.
  • This is backward compatible but permissive.

docs.title: Proposed Config
docs.text:
Add an insert policy setting:

memory:
  insert_policy: permissive

Allowed values:

  • permissive: current behavior. No save-intent marker required.
  • require_save_intent: reject inserts unless the client sends an accepted save-intent marker.
  • review_pending: store inserts without an accepted save-intent marker as pending review and exclude them from default reads until approval.

Implemented values are permissive, require_save_intent, and review_pending.

Default: permissive, to avoid breaking existing clients. Recommended mode for personal memory deployments: require_save_intent.

docs.title: Save-Intent Contract
docs.text:
Clients that intentionally save memory should include:

{
  "metadata": {
    "save_intent": "explicit_user_request"
  }
}

Accepted values:

  • explicit_user_request: user said to save, remember, store, or equivalent.
  • user_confirmed: client asked for confirmation before saving.
  • client_auto_save: user enabled an explicit client auto-save mode.

Optional supporting metadata:

{
  "metadata": {
    "save_intent": "user_confirmed",
    "save_intent_source": "opencode",
    "save_intent_evidence": "User confirmed: yes, remember that."
  }
}

Do not require clients to send raw prompt history as evidence. Evidence should be short and non-sensitive.

docs.title: P0: Server-Side Policy Enforcement
docs.text:
• [x] Add a typed config model for insert policy.
  • [x] Validate metadata.save_intent on API insert and MCP memory_insert.
  • [x] Keep permissive fully backward compatible.
  • [x] In require_save_intent, return a deterministic validation error when the marker is missing or unknown.
  • [x] Ensure errors do not echo sensitive conversation text.
  • [x] In review_pending, store the conversation with pending status and exclude it from default reads.

Suggested error shape:

{
  "status": "error",
  "error_code": "save_intent_required",
  "error_message": "memory_insert requires metadata.save_intent when memory.insert_policy is require_save_intent"
}

docs.title: P1: Pending Review Workflow
docs.text:
• [x] Add pending memory metadata status.
  • [x] Add read filters for pending, active, and rejected memories.
  • [x] Add API and MCP operations to approve or reject pending inserts.
  • [x] Prevent pending inserts from creating active facts until approved.
  • [x] Preserve audit metadata showing when the pending memory was received and approved.

docs.title: P1: Documentation And Client Guidance
docs.text:
• [x] Document the client contract in MCP setup docs.
  • [x] Tell clients not to call memory_insert for ordinary user statements unless auto-save is explicitly enabled.
  • [ ] Add suggested prompts/config notes for opencode, Codex, Claude, and other clients.
  • [x] Document require_save_intent as the recommended mode for personal deployments.
  • [x] Document permissive as a compatibility mode for trusted local workflows.

docs.title: P2: Fact-Layer Integration
docs.text:
• [x] Attach save-intent metadata to extracted facts.
  • [x] Allow fact/profile queries to filter by save-intent source.
  • [x] Include save-intent provenance in memory_ask compact provenance when facts are used.
  • [x] Consider lower confidence for facts derived from client_auto_save than explicit_user_request.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• [x] API insert without metadata.save_intent succeeds under permissive.
  • [x] MCP insert without metadata.save_intent succeeds under permissive.
  • [x] API insert without metadata.save_intent is rejected under require_save_intent.
  • [x] MCP insert without metadata.save_intent is rejected under require_save_intent.
  • [x] API and MCP inserts with explicit_user_request, user_confirmed, or client_auto_save succeed under require_save_intent.
  • [x] Unknown save-intent values are rejected with stable errors.
  • [x] review_pending stores pending data but excludes it from default search, ask, fact search, profile reads, and default retrieve.
  • [x] Pending approval activates search and fact/profile visibility.
  • [x] Validation errors do not leak payload text, auth tokens, or provider credentials.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• Users can centrally prevent unconfirmed client memory writes.
  • Existing permissive local workflows remain compatible.
  • MCP and API surfaces enforce the same policy.
  • Docs explain how clients should signal explicit memory-saving intent.
  • Regression tests cover opencode-style proactive inserts without intent markers.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Provide a simple first-run UI that helps users connect ai-memory-hub to MCP clients with Google sign-in. Google proves user identity; ai-memory-hub issues the MCP bearer token that controls memory:read and memory:write access.

User-facing setup should use api.auth: oauth_resource_server. Keep api.auth: none reserved for CI/test fixtures and maintainer-only smoke tests.

docs.title: Product Shape
docs.text:
Add a small server-rendered Connect UI, not a marketing site:

  • GET / redirects to or renders the Connect UI.
  • GET /connect shows service status, MCP URL, auth status, and client setup snippets.
  • GET /auth/google starts Google OAuth/OIDC login.
  • GET /auth/google/callback validates Google login, creates or finds the local user, creates a web session, and issues or displays the hub token workflow.
  • POST /auth/logout clears the web session.

The UI should show:

  • MCP URL, for example https://memory.example.com/mcp.
  • Signed-in identity, for example alice@example.com.
  • Copy buttons for client setup snippets.
  • Auth support status per client: verified OAuth, bearer fallback, or unverified.
  • Account-switching guidance: sign out or clear the client MCP auth token, then authenticate again.

docs.title: Storage Model
docs.text:
Use the same configured metadata database for durable auth state. SQLite remains the default local store; Postgres and other metadata providers should implement the same contract when they support auth.

Store:

  • oauth_identities
  • provider, initially google
  • provider subject, from Google sub
  • local user_id
  • normalized email and display name
  • created and last-login timestamps
  • web_sessions
  • hashed session id
  • user_id
  • CSRF token hash
  • expiry, created, last-seen, revoked timestamps
  • auth_tokens or OAuth access-token records
  • token id and hash or JWT id
  • user_id
  • scopes
  • expiry and revoked timestamps

Do not store Google access tokens by default. Store Google refresh tokens only if a later feature truly needs Google APIs; MCP authorization should use hub-issued tokens.

docs.title: Phase 1: Connect UI Skeleton
docs.text:
• [x] Add config for enabling the Connect UI, default enabled for user-facing Docker/runtime setups.
  • [x] Add public Connect UI routes that do not require MCP bearer auth: /, /connect, /auth/google, /auth/google/callback, and /auth/logout.
  • [x] Render a Jinja-backed HTML page with service status, MCP URL, and auth status. Templates and static assets live under memory/ui/connect.
  • [x] Derive the MCP URL from api.public_base_url plus /mcp unless api.oauth.resource is explicitly configured.
  • [x] Add copyable setup snippets with placeholders for Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, OpenCode, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI.
  • [x] Mark every unverified client snippet as unverified until tested against current official docs or local client behavior.
  • [x] Add tests for route availability, secret-free rendering, and correct MCP URL derivation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Google OAuth/OIDC Login
docs.text:
• [x] Add config for Google OAuth: client id env var, client secret env var, callback URL, allowed hosted domains, and allowed email list if configured.
  • [x] Use maintained Python OAuth/OIDC libraries rather than hand-rolling protocol handling.
  • [x] Start Google login from /auth/google using OIDC scopes: openid email profile.
  • [x] Validate the Google callback, ID token signature, issuer, audience, nonce, state, and expiry. Provider PKCE remains tracked in oidc_pkce_hardening_plan.md.
  • [x] Reject users outside configured hosted-domain or email allowlists.
  • [x] Never log Google tokens, ID-token claims beyond safe identifiers, or raw callback query strings.
  • [x] Add unit/integration tests for callback success, invalid state, wrong audience, expired token, denied domain, and secret redaction.

docs.title: Phase 3: Durable Identity And Web Sessions
docs.text:
• [x] Add oauth_identities metadata-store contract methods.
  • [x] Implement Google subject to local user lookup and creation.
  • [x] Add web_sessions metadata-store contract methods.
  • [x] Store only hashed session ids and hashed CSRF tokens.
  • [x] Set web-session cookies as HttpOnly, Secure when not on loopback, and SameSite=Lax.
  • [x] Make sessions survive server restart when the metadata DB and session signing secret are unchanged.
  • [x] Add logout and session revocation.
  • [ ] Add migration tests for SQLite and Postgres metadata stores.
  • [x] Add restart tests proving the same Google subject maps to the same owner_id.

docs.title: Phase 4: Hub-Issued MCP Tokens
docs.text:
• [x] Add a token issuer that creates hub-owned access tokens after Google login.
  • [x] Include sub, iss, aud or resource, scope, iat, exp, and jti claims.
  • [x] Use api.oauth.resource or api.public_base_url + /mcp as the MCP audience/resource.
  • [x] Scope default tokens to memory:read memory:write.
  • [x] Keep token expiry short by default.
  • [x] Store revocation state or token hashes where needed to support logout and emergency revocation.
  • [x] Reuse existing OAuth resource-server validation for MCP/API requests.
  • [x] Add tests for valid token use, expired token rejection, wrong resource rejection, insufficient scope, revocation, and account isolation.

docs.title: Phase 5: MCP Client Setup Matrix
docs.text:
• [x] Create a client setup matrix for: Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, OpenCode, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI.
  • [ ] For each client, document: config file path or command, exact MCP URL snippet, OAuth support status, token storage behavior, reauth/account-switch behavior, and known limits.
  • [ ] Verify exact syntax against official docs or local client behavior before marking a client as verified.
  • [x] Keep unverified clients visible but labeled Unverified.
  • [x] Include copy buttons in the Connect UI.
  • [ ] Include copy buttons in docs.
  • [x] Add tests that generated snippets include the configured MCP URL and never include raw tokens.

docs.title: Phase 6: Account Switching And Reauth
docs.text:
• [x] Document that account switching is client-driven.
  • [x] Add UI guidance for clearing the old MCP auth token before signing in with another Google account.
  • [x] Make the server treat each Google sub as a distinct identity unless an admin explicitly links accounts.
  • [x] Add a safe account-linking plan or explicitly defer account linking.
  • [x] Add tests proving User A cannot access User B memory after reauth with a different Google account.

docs.title: Phase 7: Docker And Release Docs
docs.text:
• [x] Add a user-facing OAuth-enabled Docker Compose example.
  • [x] Keep test-only unauthenticated Compose examples labeled as maintainer smoke tests.
  • [x] Document required environment variables: Google client id, Google client secret, hub JWT/session secret, api.public_base_url, and allowed domains/emails.
  • [x] Document restart behavior: identities and sessions persist with the same metadata DB and secrets; changing the JWT/session secret invalidates existing tokens/sessions.
  • [x] Update README quickstart to send users to /connect.
  • [x] Update MCP docs to make /connect the source of exact client setup snippets.

docs.title: Phase 8: Security, Privacy, And Operations
docs.text:
• [x] Add CSRF protection for state-changing UI routes.
  • [ ] Rate-limit login and callback attempts when a rate-limit mechanism exists.
  • [ ] Add audit events for login success, login denial, logout, token issuance, token revocation, and account switch.
  • [ ] Redact session ids, authorization headers, Google tokens, and hub tokens from logs, traces, metrics labels, and error responses.
  • [x] Add readiness/observability status for Connect UI and Google OAuth config without exposing secrets.
  • [x] Add a safe diagnostics panel to /connect that renders auth mode, endpoint mode, provider health, and OpenTelemetry status without memory counts, identities, bearer tokens, API keys, DSNs, raw queries, or embeddings.
  • [x] Keep /connect available when api.connect.enabled is true even when api.auth: none; render it as a local/trusted no-auth setup page instead of hiding the page.
  • [x] Render api.auth: bearer_token as a protected-header mode with client setup guidance but no secret display.
  • [x] Render api.auth: oauth_resource_server as the OAuth client-owned authorization mode, showing configured providers as non-clickable readiness chips.
  • [ ] Add negative tests for token leakage in logs and rendered pages.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Current implementation:

  • The Connect UI is server-rendered with Jinja templates under memory/ui/connect and enabled through api.connect.
  • Passport sign-in providers are configured through api.connect.passport. This is a hub config namespace, not Node Passport middleware. Google, Meta, and X are accepted provider names; live OAuth authorization and callback handling uses HTTPX plus JOSE/OIDC token verification through the oauth extra. Test hooks can still inject provider claims without calling external identity providers.
  • Google sub values map to deterministic local users. Account linking is explicitly deferred; different Google subjects stay distinct unless a future admin workflow links them.
  • Hub-issued MCP tokens are HS256 JWTs with sub, iss, aud, resource, scope, iat, exp, and jti; their hashes are also stored in auth_tokens so logout can revoke the current token.
  • Client snippets are visible. Untested clients remain Unverified until checked against current client releases; Droid is verified locally for HTTP MCP setup.

Remaining follow-ups:

  • Complete Postgres migration tests for oauth_identities and web_sessions.
  • Verify exact client setup syntax and token-storage behavior per client.
  • Add rate limiting once a shared rate-limit mechanism exists.
  • Add explicit audit-event coverage and log/rendered-page token-leakage tests.
  • Complete provider PKCE support in oidc_pkce_hardening_plan.md.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• [ ] A new user can start the OAuth-enabled Docker setup, open /connect, sign in with Google, copy an MCP URL/snippet, and connect at least one verified MCP client.
  • [ ] The MCP client sends Authorization: Bearer <hub-token> and memory reads and writes are scoped to the signed-in user.
  • [ ] Server restart preserves identities and active sessions when the metadata DB and secrets persist.
  • [ ] Reauth with another Google account maps to another local user and cannot read the previous user's memory.
  • [ ] User-facing docs do not present api.auth: none as a setup option.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Create a concrete quality gate that must pass before graph-derived memory can influence retrieval ranking or memory_ask answers.

The gate should make entity extraction, relationship extraction, provenance, and graph-aware retrieval measurable with deterministic local fixtures. This avoids promoting graph memory based on intuition alone.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• [x] Add a local benchmark module: memory.benchmarks.graph_quality.
  • [x] Define a representative golden corpus for graph-memory extraction and retrieval behavior.
  • [x] Report entity, relationship, provenance, conflict-detection, and graph-retrieval metrics.
  • [x] Fail with explicit threshold messages when graph quality is below the promotion bar.
  • [x] Keep graph retrieval disabled until the quality gate passes.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• [ ] Do not implement production graph retrieval in this plan.
  • [ ] Do not require hosted LLMs or network access.
  • [ ] Do not make graph extraction overwrite raw conversations or normalized facts.
  • [ ] Do not expose graph-derived answers through MCP/API before provenance and quality gates are in place.

docs.title: Phase 1: Golden Corpus Shape
docs.text:
• [x] Create a small deterministic corpus of representative conversations.
  • [x] Cover project-memory examples already used by the repo: Codex/opencode handoff, PGVector, bearer auth, observability, tokenizer setup, retrieval benchmarks, Velvet Lantern, tools, providers, and user preferences.
  • [x] For each conversation, define stable conversation IDs and message indexes.
  • [x] For each corpus item, define expected entities: id, type, name, aliases, source_conversation_id, source_message_index, and optional source_fact_id.
  • [x] For each corpus item, define expected relationships: subject, predicate, object, confidence, source_conversation_id, source_message_index, and optional source_fact_id.
  • [x] Include negative examples where text mentions nearby entities but should not create a relationship.
  • [x] Include conflict examples where newer memory contradicts older memory.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] The corpus is local, deterministic, and small enough for unit tests.
  • [x] Expected entities and relationships are human-readable.
  • [x] Provenance expectations are explicit instead of inferred later.

docs.title: Phase 2: Metric Definitions
docs.text:
• [x] Entity precision: matched expected entities divided by produced entities.
  • [x] Entity recall: matched expected entities divided by expected entities.
  • [x] Entity F1: harmonic mean of entity precision and recall.
  • [x] Relationship precision: matched expected relationships divided by produced relationships.
  • [x] Relationship recall: matched expected relationships divided by expected relationships.
  • [x] Relationship F1: harmonic mean of relationship precision and recall.
  • [x] Provenance accuracy: matched extracted records with correct source provenance divided by matched extracted records.
  • [x] Conflict-detection precision and recall for contradictory relationship or fact candidates.
  • [x] Graph retrieval precision_at_1, recall_at_k, and MRR for relationship questions.
  • [x] Baseline comparison against non-graph retrieval for the same graph retrieval cases.

Matching policy:

  • [x] Entity matching should normalize case, whitespace, and configured aliases.
  • [x] Relationship matching should require normalized subject, predicate, and object match.
  • [x] Provenance matching should require the expected conversation ID and message index, with chunk/fact ID checks when available.
  • [x] Extra unsupported entities or relationships count against precision.
  • [x] Missing expected entities or relationships count against recall.

docs.title: Phase 3: Benchmark Module
docs.text:
• [x] Add memory/benchmarks/graph_quality.py.
  • [x] Expose run_evaluation(...) -> dict[str, Any].
  • [x] Expose assert_thresholds(report: dict[str, Any]) -> None.
  • [x] Add a CLI entrypoint runnable as: uv run python -m memory.benchmarks.graph_quality.
  • [x] Print JSON with: corpus, entity, relationship, provenance, conflict_detection, graph_retrieval, baseline_retrieval, and thresholds sections.
  • [x] Return exit code 1 when threshold failures exist.
  • [x] Keep the benchmark independent of external storage, embeddings, LLMs, and network services.

Suggested CLI options:

  • [x] --top-k
  • [x] --min-entity-precision
  • [x] --min-entity-recall
  • [x] --min-relationship-precision
  • [x] --min-relationship-recall
  • [x] --min-provenance-accuracy
  • [x] --min-graph-precision-at-1
  • [x] --min-graph-recall-at-k
  • [x] --min-graph-mrr

docs.title: Phase 4: Initial Thresholds
docs.text:
Initial thresholds should be conservative and adjustable as fixtures become more representative.

  • [x] Entity precision must be at least 0.90.
  • [x] Entity recall must be at least 0.80.
  • [x] Relationship precision must be at least 0.95.
  • [x] Relationship recall must be at least 0.75.
  • [x] Provenance accuracy must be at least 0.98.
  • [x] Graph retrieval precision_at_1 must be at least 0.85.
  • [x] Graph retrieval recall_at_k must be at least 0.90.
  • [x] Graph retrieval MRR must be at least 0.85.
  • [x] Graph retrieval must not regress below baseline retrieval on ordinary semantic queries.
  • [x] Every threshold failure must include the metric name, observed value, and expected value.

docs.title: Phase 5: Tests
docs.text:
• [x] Add tests/unit/test_graph_quality_benchmark.py.
  • [x] Test report shape and required metric sections.
  • [x] Test invalid threshold arguments.
  • [x] Test explicit threshold failure messages.
  • [x] Test entity precision/recall/F1 calculations.
  • [x] Test relationship precision/recall/F1 calculations.
  • [x] Test provenance accuracy calculation.
  • [x] Test graph retrieval regression detection against baseline retrieval.
  • [x] Test CLI exit code behavior for passing and failing thresholds.

docs.title: Phase 6: Promotion Rule
docs.text:
• [x] Graph extraction may be developed before the gate passes, but graph-derived records must remain review-only or disabled for retrieval.
  • [x] Graph lookup may become a retrieval candidate source only after the graph quality benchmark passes agreed thresholds.
  • [x] Any new entity type, relationship predicate, extractor, or graph reranking rule must add or update benchmark cases.
  • [x] Public API/MCP graph fields must stay experimental until the benchmark and shape tests cover them.

docs.title: Done When
docs.text:
• [x] memory.benchmarks.graph_quality exists and runs locally without network dependencies.
  • [x] The benchmark reports entity, relationship, provenance, conflict, and graph-retrieval metrics.
  • [x] Threshold failures are explicit and actionable.
  • [x] Unit tests cover metric calculations and threshold failures.
  • [x] docs/improvements/advanced_memory_plan.md points to this gate before graph-aware retrieval.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Make ai-memory-hub the reliable handoff layer between agent sessions and agent clients. When one agent runs out of context, budget, time, or tool access, the next agent should be able to continue from a compact, cited, permission-aware handoff packet instead of rediscovering the task from raw chat history.

The product promise is simple: a user can mark an ordinary memory as unfinished work, then find and resume it tomorrow, next month, or after time away. A generated handoff packet may summarize that memory, but it is a view rather than a second stored resource.

If the hub is backed by reachable cloud storage or a hosted deployment, the same handoff can be resumed from local machines, cloud IDEs, remote dev containers, agent CLIs, and MCP-capable clients without copying a transcript between environments.

docs.title: Why This Is Top Priority
docs.text:
Context loss is one of the most common failure modes in real agent workflows. Users start meaningful work in Codex, opencode, Claude, Copilot, or another client, then the session runs out of context or budget. The useful work is not truly gone, but it is trapped in a conversation transcript that the next agent cannot reliably reconstruct.

Generic memory search is the foundation. Continuation needs a small, well-documented marker that lets normal search and ask focus on unfinished work.

docs.title: Design References
docs.text:
The plan borrows small, proven concepts without copying provider-specific session formats:

  • Hermes: preserve opaque source-client and source-session identity plus the workspace/project scope used to find the work again.
  • Codex: preserve immutable parent lineage so a continuation can point to the memory it follows without rewriting history.
  • OpenCode: generate a compact resume hint from the underlying memory while retaining that memory as the source of truth.

These are metadata conventions on ordinary memories. They do not authorize the hub to replay a foreign session, import provider credentials, or inherit the source agent's permissions.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• [x] Represent a stored handoff as an ordinary memory with metadata.handoff_at.
  • [x] Preserve the current MCP and HTTP memory surfaces; do not add a parallel handoff CRUD API.
  • [x] Query unfinished work through normal memory_search and memory_ask using handoff_only=true.
  • [x] Make handoff packets compact enough for low-budget agents to consume.
  • [ ] Make handoffs portable across local, LAN, hosted, and cloud development environments when the same authenticated hub is reachable.
  • [x] Keep handoff reads scoped by owner, project, shared-project membership, and existing auth policy.
  • [x] Keep A2A protocol support optional and later; implement the core handoff value over MCP and HTTP first.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• [ ] Do not replace conversation memory, facts, profile memory, or raw message storage.
  • [x] Do not let one agent hand off private project context to another agent without the same authorization checks used by search and ask.
  • [x] Do not treat retrieved handoff text as executable instructions.
  • [x] Do not expose secrets, raw tokens, DSNs, environment dumps, or private tool output in generated handoff packets.
  • [x] Do not require A2A before the handoff model is useful.

docs.title: Handoff Memory Model
docs.text:
Persisted fields are intentionally small and live in ordinary memory metadata:

  • [x] handoff_at: RFC 3339 timestamp marking the memory as unfinished work.
  • [x] project_id: existing project/workspace authorization scope.
  • [x] source_client: optional producer such as codex, hermes, opencode, or gemini; treat it as descriptive provenance, not authority.
  • [x] source_session_id: optional opaque identifier from the source client.
  • [x] Keep project_id as the workspace identity; representative repository fixtures do not justify adding a separate workspace_key contract.
  • [x] parent_conversation_id: optional immutable link to the preceding memory in a continuation chain. CLI output retains parent_memory_id as a public compatibility alias; it is not a second persisted field.
  • [x] resume_hint: compact, cited continuation guidance generated from the underlying authorized memory.

The richer packet returned by result_mode="handoff" remains an ephemeral view. It may contain goal, summary, decisions, changed files, commands, validation, blockers, next steps, citations, confidence, and completeness notes without turning those fields into a second persistence model.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] Handoff views are compact, structured, and readable by humans and agents.
  • [x] Every generated packet links back to evidence instead of being an unsupported summary.
  • [x] A new agent can request "what was happening here?" and receive a useful continuation packet in one call.

docs.title: Phase 1: Retrieval-Only Handoff View
docs.text:
• [x] Add internal handoff packet generation from authorized conversation chunks and summaries; fact-layer expansion remains optional future work.
  • [x] Add deterministic extraction templates for continuation packets.
  • [x] Include explicit source citations and confidence notes.
  • [x] Add result_mode="handoff" as a read-only ask option if it can fit the existing response shape without breaking clients.
  • [x] Keep generated packets ephemeral until the user or agent explicitly saves them.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] No schema migration is required for the first read-only view.
  • [x] Existing memory_ask and search behavior remains backward compatible.
  • [x] Handoff generation refuses to include redacted or unauthorized memory.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stored Handoff Marker
docs.text:
• [x] Add optional metadata.handoff_at to the ordinary conversation schema.
  • [x] Define presence of handoff_at as “unfinished work saved for later.”
  • [x] Add handoff_only to existing HTTP and MCP search/ask requests.
  • [x] Keep insert, retrieve, authorization, redaction, indexing, and storage on the normal memory path.
  • [ ] Add a later resolution/link field only when a proven resume workflow requires it; do not introduce a parallel handoff lifecycle prematurely.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] API and MCP responses remain the existing memory response envelopes.
  • [x] Handoffs can be saved explicitly at the end of a session.
  • [x] Handoffs can be resumed explicitly at the start of a later session.
  • [x] Handoff memories inherit normal memory authorization and audit behavior.

docs.title: Phase 3: Source Provenance And Workspace Identity
docs.text:
• [x] Add optional metadata.source_client without restricting clients to a closed provider enum.
  • [x] Add optional opaque metadata.source_session_id; never interpret it as a credential or proof of access.
  • [x] Reuse project_id as the primary workspace boundary.
  • [x] Do not add workspace_key without representative evidence that project_id cannot distinguish a supported workflow.
  • [x] Document client mappings for Hermes, Codex, and OpenCode session IDs.
  • [x] Ensure concise responses expose useful provenance without leaking local paths or private provider identifiers by default.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] A memory created in Codex can be found from another client by project and source provenance.
  • [x] Missing provenance fields do not affect existing memory behavior.
  • [x] Source identifiers remain descriptive metadata and never bypass normal owner/project authorization.

docs.title: Phase 4: Immutable Continuation Lineage
docs.text:
• [x] Use optional metadata.parent_conversation_id as the canonical persisted field referencing an authorized memory.
  • [x] Validate that parent and child belong to the same visible project scope.
  • [x] Keep parent memories immutable; continuation creates a new memory rather than rewriting its predecessor.
  • [x] Return lineage bounded to 16 ancestors in detailed retrieval and handoff views, with explicit truncation, missing-history, and cycle markers.
  • [x] Detect missing, cyclic, over-depth, or cross-project lineage deterministically with stable lineage_* error codes.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] A continuation from one client can point back to the authorized memory it resumed in another client.
  • [x] The complete bounded chain remains auditable without requiring either provider's native session format.
  • [x] Lineage cannot expose a parent memory the caller is not allowed to read.

docs.title: Phase 5: Compact Resume Hint
docs.text:
• [x] Generate resume_hint from the authorized underlying memory, not only from client-supplied text.
  • [x] Keep the hint short enough for low-budget agents and include source-memory citations or an explicit low-confidence result.
  • [x] Prefer read-time generation initially; persist a hint only when cache or offline workflow evidence justifies it.
  • [x] Include current objective, confirmed progress, blocker, and immediate next action when supported by evidence.
  • [x] Never treat a resume hint as executable instructions or as a replacement for retrieving the source memory.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [x] A receiving agent can orient itself without replaying the full source transcript.
  • [x] The hint stays within a documented 512-token default context budget.
  • [x] Stale or unsupported hints are clearly identified and can be regenerated.

docs.title: Phase 6: Agent Workflow Integration
docs.text:
• [x] Add MCP prompt create_handoff for "save my current working state."
  • [x] Add MCP prompt resume_handoff for "continue this task."
  • [x] Add client-facing docs for Codex, opencode, Claude, Copilot, and other MCP clients.
  • [x] Add CLI commands:
    • [x] aim handoff create
    • [x] aim handoff get
    • [x] aim handoff search
    • [x] aim handoff update
  • [ ] Add Connect UI snippets or setup guidance only after at least one real client flow is verified.
